The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
// RPS pm interrupts are cleared and disabled on module load
// Presumption that they remain disabled forevermore
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the code assumes that once the RPS interrupts are cleared and disabled during module load, they will remain disabled indefinitely. However, during the suspend process, the mask is cleared, which can lead to the RPS interrupts being unexpectedly re-enabled upon resume, causing issues in the graphics driver operation.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
intel_rps_sanitize(&gt->rps);
```
Reason:
The addition of `intel_rps_sanitize(&gt->rps);` in the `gt_sanitize` function ensures that the RPS interrupts are explicitly sanitized (i.e., cleared and disabled) upon resume. This guarantees that any interrupts that may have been re-enabled during the suspend process are properly handled, preventing unexpected behavior in the graphics driver.
